evidence.excerpt: Honeywell, Nov 2025: Jim (James) Currier named President and Chief Executive Officer of Honeywell Aerospace; president and CEO of Honeywell Aerospace Technologies since August 2023, almost two decades in senior Honeywell roles. Form 10-12B: James Currier, 60, President and CEO since the spin-off.

Honeywell, 5 Jun 2026: the Board set 15 June 2026 as the record date for the spin-off of Honeywell Aerospace; distribution expected at 12:01 a.m. New York time on 29 June 2026 at one Honeywell Aerospace share for every two Honeywell shares; when-issued trading on Nasdaq as HONAV from on or about 15 June, regular-way trading as HONA from 29 June; a Honeywell reverse stock split accompanies the separation. Investing.com (5 Jun) confirms.

Honeywell fourth-quarter 2025 release (29 Jan 2026) and the Aerospace 8-K: Aerospace Technologies 2025 net sales $17,404 million, up 13% reported and 12% organic versus 2024, led by commercial aftermarket and defence and space; fourth-quarter organic growth 21%.

Honeywell, Jan 2026: Josh Jepsen joins Honeywell Aerospace as Chief Financial Officer effective 23 February 2026, previously SVP and CFO of Deere & Company; Bob Buddecke, Dave Marinick and Rich DeGraff lead the business units reporting to Currier. No chief marketing officer is named in this release, the Nov 2025 release or the Form 10 executive-officer list as summarised.

Honeywell, Nov 2025: Craig Arnold, former Chairman and CEO of Eaton Corporation and lead director at Medtronic, to serve as non-executive Board Chair of Honeywell Aerospace on completion of the spin-off.

Honeywell, 3 Mar 2026: Form 10 registration statement filed with the SEC for the planned spin-off of Honeywell Aerospace, to be headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona, and listed on Nasdaq (Flight Global, Dealroom coverage).

Aerospace Testing International and Honeywell Aerospace's own pages: Honeywell's 1-megawatt generator for hybrid-electric aircraft operated at 1.02 MVA and ran continuously at 900 kW, at about 97% efficiency and roughly 8 kW/kg; the machine can also be used as a 1-megawatt motor without modification; paired with the HGT1700 APU it forms a turbogenerator that runs on biofuel, jet fuel or diesel.

Sponsor table (spec/active_sponsor_db.md §2, data/teams.json): Aston Martin Aramco — Aramco title (through 2028), Honda power unit from 2026, Atlas Air (cargo airline), Arm, CoreWeave, NetApp, Cognizant, ServiceNow; Bombardier listed as departed. BWT Alpine — Boeing (active). No aerospace engines, avionics or propulsion supplier is on any live F1 roster.

2026 F1 calendar table with dates from silverstone.co.uk and RacingNews365: Austrian GP on 28 June, British GP at Silverstone on 5 July 2026; United States GP (Austin) in late October and Las Vegas GP in November; Miami GP in May.

brief.ticker: Nasdaq: HONA (regular-way from 29 Jun 2026; HONAV when-issued from 15 Jun)
brief.deck: Honeywell Aerospace, the $17.4B-revenue avionics, engines and electrification supplier, becomes a standalone Nasdaq company on 29 June 2026: Honeywell's board set the 15 June record date on 5 June, and the separation gives one of aviation's biggest suppliers its own balance sheet, ticker and brand budget for the first time.
brief.the_case_p1: Honeywell announced on 5 June that its board has set 15 June 2026 as the record date for the spin-off of Honeywell Aerospace, with distribution on 29 June on a one-for-two basis; the shares trade when-issued as HONAV from around 15 June and regular-way on Nasdaq as HONA from 29 June. The business reported 2025 net sales of $17.4B, up 12% organically, led by commercial aftermarket and defence. Headquartered in Phoenix, it is led by Jim Currier as President and CEO with Josh Jepsen as CFO, chaired by former Eaton chief Craig Arnold.
brief.the_case_p2: Aerospace is already on the grid: Boeing sits on the Alpine, Atlas Air on the Aston Martin, and Bombardier, a Honeywell customer, has left the Aston Martin roster. The engines-and-avionics tier has never taken a seat. That leaves a supplier-grade engineering story, from megawatt electric machines to thermal management, without a grid home just as Formula 1's new hybrid era begins and a British team starts its Honda power-unit years.
brief.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  Regular-way trading starts 29 June, the day after the Austrian GP; the British GP on 5 July is the company's first race weekend as an independent listing. A spin-off's first hundred days set its brand, and the marketing budget is now Honeywell Aerospace's own to spend.
brief.why_team_label: WHY ASTON MARTIN ARAMCO F1 TEAM
brief.why_team_para: Aston Martin is the one team where an aerospace supplier's story is already on the car: Aramco as title partner, Honda supplying the power unit from 2026, Atlas Air in the cargo-aviation lane, Arm and CoreWeave on compute. Bombardier's business-jet slot has departed, so the aerospace-engineering lane at Silverstone is open. Honeywell's 1-megawatt generator, about 97% efficient and usable as a motor, speaks to the hybrid era better than any consumer brand could.
brief.value_section_label: VALUE TO ASTON MARTIN ARAMCO F1 TEAM
brief.value_content: MODE B - brand launch with an engineering exchange. The car carries the new company's name through its first hundred days as a listing; hospitality at the British GP and the US rounds hosts airline, defence and investor guests. Outside the regulated power unit, Honeywell's electrical-machine and thermal-management engineers work with the Silverstone campus on cooling and test rigs: aerospace-grade know-how for the team, a technical story for Honeywell.
brief.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Aerospace Technology Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, 2027-2029, the company's first three years as a listed business. Estimated $5-8M a year. Scope: sidepod placement, the engineering exchange above, hospitality at the British GP and the US rounds for airline, defence and investor guests.
brief.decision_maker_bio: Currier, 60, has run Honeywell's aerospace business since August 2023 and led it into the spin-off. Path: Josh Jepsen, CFO since February 2026 (ex-Deere), and business-unit presidents Bob Buddecke, Dave Marinick and Rich DeGraff. No chief marketing officer is named in the spin-off filings.
brief.opening_angle_intro: Lead with the first race weekend as an independent company.
brief.opening_angle_quote: “Jim, Honeywell Aerospace trades on its own from 29 June and the British GP is its first race weekend as a listed company. Aston Martin's aerospace lane is open and the hybrid era needs your electrification story. 25 minutes before the record date?”

why_now.label: Trigger
why_now.text: On 5 June 2026 Honeywell's board set 15 June as the record date for the spin-off of Honeywell Aerospace and confirmed distribution at 12:01 a.m. New York time on 29 June, one Honeywell Aerospace share for every two Honeywell shares. When-issued trading as HONAV starts on or about 15 June; regular-way trading on Nasdaq as HONA on 29 June. The Form 10 was filed on 3 March.

why_now.label: A brand that must stand on its own
why_now.text: Until 29 June the aerospace business has been a segment of a conglomerate; from that day it has its own investors, its own annual report and its own marketing budget. Spin-offs spend their first hundred days establishing an identity with investors, customers and recruits, and that is the budget a team partnership would come from.

why_now.label: Scale, honestly
why_now.text: The business reported 2025 net sales of $17.4B, up 12% organically, led by commercial aftermarket and defence and space. Capacity is not the question; appetite is. No Honeywell Formula 1 sponsorship is on record and no chief marketing officer is named, which is why the score stops at 71 despite a hard listing date inside the window.

why_now.label: Calendar window
why_now.text: Regular-way trading begins the day after the Austrian GP on 28 June; the British GP on 5 July is the first race weekend as an independent company, at the home of the recommended team. The United States GP in Austin and the Las Vegas GP follow in the autumn near the Phoenix headquarters and the US investor base.

why_team.label: The open lane
why_team.text: Aston Martin Aramco carries Aramco as title partner, Honda supplying the power unit from 2026, Atlas Air in the cargo-aviation lane, and Arm, CoreWeave, NetApp, Cognizant and ServiceNow on technology. Bombardier, a business-jet maker and Honeywell customer, has departed, so no aerospace-engineering brand is on the car: Official Aerospace Technology Partner is a clean category.

why_team.label: The only aerospace-shaped roster
why_team.text: Boeing sits on the Alpine, which closes that car to a supplier that sells to Boeing and its rivals alike. No other team carries an aerospace or aviation story on the livery; Aston Martin already has one through Atlas Air and its former business-jet partnership, so the audience and the hospitality format exist.

why_team.label: The hybrid-era engineering story
why_team.text: Formula 1's 2026 rules lean harder on the electrical side of the power unit. Honeywell's 1-megawatt aerospace generator ran at 1.02 MVA and 900 kW continuously at about 97% efficiency and roughly 8 kW/kg, and doubles as a motor. The regulated power unit is Honda's, but thermal management, test rigs and electrical engineering exchange with the Silverstone campus are open ground.

why_team.label: UK and US at once
why_team.text: A Phoenix-headquartered, Nasdaq-listed company with a British team gives the US rounds a home-market story and the British GP a first-weekend stage; Honeywell Aerospace's UK sites and European airline customers give the Silverstone hospitality a customer list.

value.label: Brand launch (Mode B)
value.text: A new listed company's identity told through precision engineering on a global broadcast in its first hundred days: the Honeywell Aerospace name on the car from the British GP, the first race weekend after the 29 June listing, with the US rounds in Austin and Las Vegas timed to the first results as an independent company.

value.label: Engineering exchange, outside the regulated unit
value.text: Thermal-management and electrical-machine know-how from the 1-megawatt generator programme applied to test rigs, cooling and energy-store integration at the AMR Technology Campus, with the homologated power unit left to Honda; a joint engineering series for the team's channels.

value.label: Commercial lift for the team
value.text: Airline, defence, business-aviation and institutional-investor guests at the British GP and the US rounds, the audience Aston Martin's Aramco and technology partners already court, plus a reference story for the team's own aerospace-grade supply chain.

value.label: What the team gives back
value.text: Official Aerospace Technology Partner designation, sidepod placement, British GP and US-round hospitality, driver and engineering access, and a first-year brand-launch activation timed to the 29 June listing.

# Honeywell Aerospace → Aston Martin Aramco F1 Team — verification log (N° 199, 9 Jun 2026)

Built in-session at no API cost (no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the sandbox) with Claude acting as
scanner, verifier and writer through the pipeline's injectable stages; the calendar table, sponsor

**Sandbox limitation, stated plainly:** direct fetches of honeywell.com, investor.honeywell.com,
sec.gov and prnewswire.com were blocked by the egress proxy. Each claim below was checked against the
search summary of the primary page named as the evidence URL. Treat every VERIFIED line as REPORTED
until a person opens the link. Confidence is MEDIUM and the footer reads VERIFY BEFORE CIRCULATION.

## The trigger, re-dated

The thin row cited a valuesense.io aggregator and "Form 10-12B". The Form 10 was filed on 3 Mar 2026,
98 days before the row date and therefore outside the 90-day window, and the separation itself
(29 Jun) and the board approval (15 Jun) fall after the row date. The trigger inside the window is
Honeywell's release of **5 Jun 2026** setting the 15 Jun record date, the 29 Jun distribution, the
one-for-two ratio and the HONAV/HONA trading dates (Investing.com confirms, 5 Jun). Nothing dated
after 9 Jun is used in the brief.

## Score: 71, value section on, two risks

The thin row said 69, and a first pass anchored on it. Re-scored against the spec's own rubric:
a dated listing (29 Jun, 20 days from the row) is a hard external date, so timing 17 and urgency 13
rather than 16 and 12; capacity is obvious ($17.4B 2025 sales). What holds it back is unchanged:
brand fit is a B2B/B2G halo (12), no marketing owner is named, and the power unit is Honda's and
homologated, so the workstream is an engineering exchange around the regulated unit rather than
product on the car (ops fit 11). The value section is therefore MODE B (brand launch) with a bounded
engineering exchange, not an operational claim. The pipeline's production gate (`MD_THRESHOLD`, 70)
is unchanged; a 69 would not have produced a record.
